title: Part History wording with and without a note, one entry per part in bulk
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Parts -> Inventory page on the build under test, with permission to view inventory parts.
  2. You hold the "Part Library & Inventory - Delete" permission (needed to change status/tracking).
  3. A selection of forty-plus parts to change in bulk.
custom_steps:
1. Deactivate with a note and read the history entry; deactivate another with no note and read its entry.
  2. Change a part's status twice and compare the status note on the part record with the history.
  3. Bulk-change 40+ parts with one note and count the history entries written.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • With a note the entry reads "Deactivated | Reason: {note}"; with no note it reads "Deactivated" and nothing else (no trailing separator).
  • The status note on the part record is the most recent one only (history keeps every change, so the two need not agree after more than one change); a bulk change over forty parts writes forty history entries, one per part, each carrying the same note.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; "Parts Lifecycle Update" PRD (Confluence 829227015, IN REVIEW 2026-09-09), Story 10 (Confirming & recording a status change); design canvas Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026 against an IN-REVIEW spec; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R17: “When the user gave a note, the entry reads "Deactivated | Reason: {note}". When the note was left empty it reads "Deactivated" and nothing else, with no trailing separator.”
  • S10-R18: “The status note held on the part record itself is the most recent one only. The history is the record of every change, and the two are not expected to agree once a part has changed status more than once.”
  • S10-R19: “A bulk change over forty parts writes forty history entries, one per part, each carrying the same note.”
